name: Flinders Coastal Walk
signature: A rugged cliff-edge walk east from Flinders village — basalt platforms, Mushroom Reef, and a stretch of coast most visitors never reach
editorNote:
The Flinders Coastal Walk runs east from the pier along the cliff edge and rock platforms toward Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary — a 3km return walk along one of the most geologically dramatic coastlines on the Peninsula. The basalt columns, rock arches, and blow holes en route are worth stopping for repeatedly.

Mushroom Reef is the natural endpoint — a protected marine sanctuary where the rock platforms at low tide are extraordinary. The walk is largely unformed and requires some scrambling at points; not suitable for small children on the rock sections.

Best at low tide when the platforms are accessible. Works in any weather — a 15-knot onshore wind actually improves the experience on this stretch of coast.
whyWeGo: The most geological walk on the Peninsula — basalt platforms, blow holes, and a marine sanctuary at the end.
ifOnlyOneThing: Time it to arrive at Mushroom Reef at low tide. Bring a mask and snorkel.

walk.difficulty: moderate — some scrambling on rock platforms
